# Tako

> Tako is a data intelligence platform. The Tako MCP server lets AI agents search a proprietary, continuously-updated knowledge base of 100K+ curated charts (latest reported quarter, same-day market prices, official releases as they publish), get grounded answers, explore Tako's data graph, fetch underlying source content, and run a multi-step Answer Agent.

## Documentation

- [MCP Server Setup](https://github.com/TakoData/tako-mcp): Connect to the hosted Tako MCP server
- [API Reference](https://tako.com/docs/): Full REST API documentation
- [Chart Gallery](https://tako.com/gallery): Browse example charts and visualizations
- [OpenAPI Spec](https://tako.com/openapi.yaml): Machine-readable API specification

## Quick Start

Connect your MCP client to `https://mcp.tako.com/mcp`. No credentials are required to start: an anonymous connection gets the free tier (`tako_search`, `tako_answer`, `tako_available_data`; 10 requests/min per IP; on ChatGPT, `tako_contents` and `tako_visualize` are also listed but require sign-in to run). For the full toolset and your own limits, authenticate with `Authorization: Bearer <TAKO_API_TOKEN>` (config-file clients) or the server's OAuth flow (Claude Code plugin, Claude.ai, ChatGPT).

Some tools are opt-in — off by default to keep the tool surface small. Enable them via `?tools=` on the URL (comma-separated aliases): `agent` (Answer Agent), `visualize` (chart authoring; already on by default for ChatGPT and Claude), `credits` (credit balance), `graph` (low-level graph primitives). Example: `https://mcp.tako.com/mcp?tools=agent,visualize`.

## Capabilities

- `tako_search` — fast, direct retrieval of a data point as structured cards (each with a free row preview; the top card auto-renders inline as a chart (interactive widget on ChatGPT, chart image on other hosts)), from Tako's curated data and the live web. Built to fan out: fire many narrow one-entity+one-metric queries in parallel rather than one broad query. Replaces a generic web search for data lookups.
- `tako_answer` — ask one specific, self-contained data question and get one synthesized answer grounded in the cards it cites. Use `tako_search` when you want the data itself, or for broad/multi-part questions.
- `tako_available_data` — find what proprietary, structured data exists on any entity or metric, as a natural-language summary. Best for a "what structured data is there on X?" question, and a cheap accuracy check to confirm a specific figure exists (and its exact name) before spending a priced `tako_search` / `tako_answer`. Each match carries a `node_id` you can pin to ground the follow-up. Free and fast.
- `tako_contents` — fetch the full rows (CSV/JSON) behind a Tako card, or the extracted text behind a web result — the step after search when you need the real data. Call it only on cards marked `exportable: true` (web URLs always work).
- `tako_visualize` — create an embeddable chart/card from your own structured data (opt-in, enable with `?tools=visualize`; on by default for ChatGPT and Claude).
- `tako_agent` — run a multi-step Answer Agent for open-ended, figure-it-out questions (opt-in, enable with `?tools=agent`; on ChatGPT the server splits this into the `tako_agent_start` / `tako_agent_wait` pair).
- `get_credit_balance` — check API credit balance (opt-in, enable with `?tools=credits`).
- `tako_graph_search` / `tako_graph_related` / `tako_graph_node` — low-level graph primitives for power users: traversal relations (siblings, members, `rel:*` edges), in-relation filtering, cursor paging, and full node detail — beyond what `tako_available_data` covers (opt-in, enable with `?tools=graph`).
